meta.source_dashboard: MANTIS ALPHA PHARMA ws 2.7.1, CAPR two-phase event correction, 2026-08-31
meta.note: Rows reconstructed from the inline dashboard script (audit, overrides, new candidates, decisions). Base rows from data.json were not available; fields marked provisional come from the reconstruction and should be confirmed against data.json.

factors.label: Contract manufacturing and CMC
factors.desc: Third party facility or CMC exposure. The dominant failure vector for otherwise approvable drugs (Camurus, Savara, Achieve, Unicycive). Playbook open item: raise the maximum deduction.

factors.label: Prior regulatory letter
factors.desc: A discount rather than a veto. Weighted more heavily when the letter went to efficacy than to a facility, because efficacy questions do not fully retire.

factors.label: Efficacy or SAP dispute with FDA
factors.desc: Sponsor publicly contesting the agency's analysis. Treated as a hard stop: the catalyst becomes a coin flip on procedure, which the model does not price.

factors.label: Advisory committee scheduled
factors.desc: Two binaries, not one. The briefing document (about two business days before the meeting) is the tradeable event. Effective exit resets to that date less three business days.

factors.label: Crowded field or approved competitor
factors.desc: Flattens run-ups even when the catalyst is clean. Mineralys and Vera are the reference cases.

factors.label: Large capitalisation or already priced
factors.desc: Dilutes the catalyst until the event stops being the company. Consensus has already paid for a clean package.

factors.label: Move already made
factors.desc: A stock that has already re-rated has spent the move the trade was meant to capture. Reframe from accumulation to exit management; no chase.

factors.label: Financing, liquidity or listing risk
factors.desc: Cash runway under four quarters past the action date is a live dilution risk. A raise inside the window ends the run-up. Thin books fail the tradability gate.

factors.label: Partner is the applicant
factors.desc: Milestone and royalty economics dilute direct catalyst sensitivity.

factors.label: International listing
factors.desc: Needs the international template: Stockholm or Euronext liquidity, FX exposure and disclosure rules before sharing the domestic rubric.

factors.label: Surrogate endpoint or accelerated pathway
factors.desc: Procedural risk around accelerated approval eligibility, novel surrogates and historical controls.

factors.label: Same issuer, second catalyst
factors.desc: Separate asset, same balance sheet and management. Score and size must reflect aggregate issuer exposure; it is not a second full strength position.

factors.label: Extension reset
factors.desc: A three month move on a major amendment unwinds positioned holders mechanically and opens a fresh accumulation window on the reset calendar. Praxis is the reference case.

factors.label: Structural fit filter (mechanical exclusion)
factors.desc: Removed on listing and liquidity grounds, not by clinical scoring. The model cannot claim credit for these outcomes.

catalysts.ind: SCN2A and SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
catalysts.notes: Extended three months on 29 June. FDA classified additional sensitivity analyses as a major amendment; no new studies requested, no safety or manufacturing concerns cited. Extension reset is the defined entry trigger, but the issuer is now large and already substantially re-rated, and the second Praxis catalyst caps aggregate issuer exposure.

factors.note: 27 Sep to 27 Dec on a 29 Jun filing

catalysts.notes: Separate asset but the same issuer, balance sheet and management. Score and size must reflect aggregate Praxis exposure. Drug and indication reconstructed; confirm against data.json.

Extended three months; responses to FDA information requests deemed a major amendment. No advisory committee planned. Follows a May 2025 refuse to file on CMC, after which drug substance manufacture moved to Fujifilm. CMC history, a larger valuation and a well known positive narrative reduce the remaining attention premium. Manage, do not chase.

factors.note: May 2025 refuse to file on CMC; Fujifilm transfer

catalysts.notes: Strong catalyst but a large current valuation and two applications for the same molecule reduce independent torque. A third filing (AdvSM, submitted 30 June) has no date yet.
Second decision for the same molecule and issuer; it cannot be treated as a second full strength position.

Baxdrostat is already approved first in class and sell side consensus sits near ninety per cent, so there is very little uncertainty premium left to harvest even though the drug is probably fine. Reference case for an uncontested package.

catalysts.ind: Kidney transplant desensitisation in highly sensitised patients
catalysts.notes: Promoted from blanket exclusion into the international template. First in class, exact date catalyst, but the stock is near its 52 week high after a strong one month move. Do not chase. Apply Stockholm liquidity, SEK and disclosure rules. Priority review was requested but a standard 12 month cycle was assigned.
Exceptional Phase 3 RINGSIDE efficacy supports the filing, but Ogsiveo is already approved and the competitive benchmark limits the novelty premium.

catalysts.ind: Pain associated with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis
catalysts.notes: Small cap torque and three large randomised trials are attractive. Non orphan knee OA, biologic classification, manufacturing and mass market commercial assumptions need bespoke diligence.

catalysts.ind: Duchenne muscular dystrophy, refined upper limb indication
catalysts.mantis_class: Special situation watch, no re-entry veto
catalysts.notes: Two phase control case. CTGTAC voted 9 to 3 against on 29 July on the cardiomyopathy question; the thesis broke on the 27 July briefing document, which is where the exit should have fired (effective exit 24 July, 22 days earlier than the calendar rule). Bloomberg ledger use case loss 26.00 per cent, closed 23 July. FDA accepted 24 month HOPE-3 data as a major amendment on 24 August and moved the date to 22 November. The SAP v1.1 versus v3.0 dispute remains a no re-entry veto; the approximately 90 per cent extension path rebound on 14 August is archived separately and not netted.

catalysts.ind: Duchenne muscular dystrophy amenable to exon 51 skipping
catalysts.notes: Original Score 4 pre pre PDUFA cycle locked at 3.37 per cent (3 Aug to 27 Aug close). Accelerated approval filing on dystrophin as a surrogate. A fresh position faces a multi billion dollar valuation and surrogate endpoint risk; require a reset before re-entry.

factors.note: cycle A locked at 3.37 per cent

catalysts.ind: On demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks
catalysts.notes: Original Score 4 cycle locked at 14.73 per cent (3 Aug to 27 Aug close). The HAE thesis remains attractive, but competition and the August re-rating reduce fresh entry torque.

factors.note: cycle A locked at 14.73 per cent

catalysts.notes: Original Score 4 cycle locked at 49.82 per cent (3 Aug to 27 Aug close). BLA accepted 15 June with no filing review issues; would be the first systemic therapy in the indication. The August re-rating makes a fresh entry a no chase setup.

factors.note: cycle A locked at 49.82 per cent

catalysts.notes: First potential STGD1 treatment, Priority Review, multiple expedited designations and a positive Phase 3 DRAGON study (35.7 per cent reduction in lesion growth). The company has already substantially re-rated and carries a multi billion dollar valuation, limiting classic torque. Track rather than chase.
Small enough for torque, but Taiho is the applicant and partnership economics dilute the direct binary exposure. Based on Phase 2b REZILIENT1.

No advisory committee planned. FDA flagged a potential review issue: a preliminary view that accelerated approval eligibility is not adequately justified. Micro cap financing and listing risk dominate the catalyst.

catalysts.ind: EGFR mutant NSCLC after TKI, with chemotherapy
catalysts.notes: First US BLA acceptance for a PD-1 and VEGF bispecific. Mid cycle and wrap up meetings, no ODAC scheduled. The issuer is valued above the classic torque range and much of the narrative is priced.

Company defining rare disease catalyst, offset by the prior CMC complete response history and issuer level correlation. The separate DTX401 filing was approved 19 August (GENGLYCOS). Window is mature: at T-12 today, execution belongs to exit management, not accumulation.

Strong programme, but a large diversified issuer provides limited binary equity torque. Bepirovirsen (chronic hepatitis B, GSK led) is reported at 26 Oct with lower confidence; olezarsen sHTG already approved 24 June.

catalysts.ind: Papillary NMIBC without carcinoma in situ
catalysts.notes: Supplemental filing at a multi billion dollar issuer, not a company defining first approval. Review focuses on whether the CIS to papillary extrapolation is justified. A public workshop was held 18 May, not an advisory committee.
Unusually clean drug and regulatory setup with no AdCom planned, but a large commercial stage issuer offers little classic binary torque.

catalysts.ind: Prevention of surgical site infection after abdominal colorectal surgery
catalysts.notes: Strong package and no filing issues identified, but market depth and financing dependence fail the tradability gate. Track as a control, not a live position.

catalysts.ind: At home acute agitation in bipolar disorder or schizophrenia
catalysts.notes: Potentially meaningful label expansion, but low cash, strategic alternatives language and financing risk dominate the catalyst. Financial survivability veto.

catalysts.ind: Tau PET imaging in Alzheimer disease
catalysts.notes: Action date has passed. Outcome not yet recorded in the dashboard; confirm approval or otherwise from a primary source before reclassifying.
Company disclosed August 2026 as a month only. The 30 Sep figure on aggregator calendars is an end of quarter placeholder. Month has passed; outcome to confirm.

catalysts.ind: Open angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension
catalysts.notes: Exact date and two positive Phase 3 studies merit tracking, but Nicox is Euronext listed and Kowa owns the US filing. Milestone and royalty economics dilute direct catalyst sensitivity.

Rare disease and Breakthrough fit is strong, but the filing relies on a novel surrogate and the accelerated pathway. No live score until the complete BLA is accepted and an exact action date is issued.
Potentially high attention gene therapy catalyst, but FDA position reversals and the historical control debate create procedural risk. Track the filing; no live position before formal acceptance.
Strong Phase 3 X-TOLE2 efficacy and a differentiated mechanism qualify it for future scoring. Wait for NDA acceptance, exact date, filing classification and a valuation review.

catalysts.notes: Approved 26 March 2026. Calibration anchor for a clean setup. Record integrity: the run-up has been logged at both 46.32 and 47.51 per cent; reconcile to one sourced figure with a stated window before external use.

catalysts.ind: Primary IgA nephropathy at risk of progression
catalysts.catalyst_type: BLA, accelerated approval, Breakthrough, Priority Review
catalysts.mantis_class: Reference case, crowded field and hostile macro
catalysts.notes: Approved 7 July 2026. The framework flagged three adverse signals in advance (declining 200 day average, crowded IgAN field, sector risk off) and had no mechanism to act on any of them. This case created the thesis deterioration exit rule.

record.window: entry 17 Jan to 15 Mar 2026, exit 28 May to 30 Jun 2026

catalysts.notes: Acquired by GSK at 124 dollars a share. Leaves the run-up pool and becomes a spread trade with different mechanics. Drug and indication reconstructed.
Approved 27 August 2026. Catalyst completed and archived. Priority review did not overcome a very large issuer valuation and diversified exposure.
Approved 19 August 2026, four days ahead of the action date.
Gilead closed the acquisition 28 April 2026; the ticker no longer trades. The action date stands but the exposure is now GILD. Removed from the tradable watchlist.
Approved 25 June 2026 ahead of the 30 June date. The follow on subcutaneous VRDN-003 BLA is guided for year end and has no date yet.

catalysts.ind: HR positive, HER2 negative, PIK3CA wild type advanced breast cancer
catalysts.notes: Approved 14 July 2026 ahead of the 17 July date. Added to NCCN guidelines 30 July. Catalyst spent.

catalysts.ind: Oedema in heart failure; paediatric diabetes
catalysts.notes: Both 2026 actions cleared: Afrezza paediatric 29 May and Furoscix ReadyFlow 24 July. No further dated catalyst; MNKD-101 is still Phase 3.

CRL 22 June 2026: cGMP deficiencies at a third party facility plus incomplete labelling. No efficacy or clinical safety deficiencies. Resubmission guided for Q4 2026, approval possible H1 2027. Facility grounds: discount, not veto, on the next cycle.
Second CRL 30 June 2026, same third party CMC deficiencies as the first. No clinical issues raised. No new action date announced.

catalysts.notes: Two letters on the same third party inspection with a drug already approved in Europe. Removed by the structural fit filter on listing and liquidity grounds, not by clinical scoring. Also the reference case for a missed entry window.
Failed on manufacturing after being removed mechanically by the structural fit filter. The model cannot claim credit for the outcome.
